nodes.label: Codex Efficiency Fixes Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Ship the five evidence-strong treatments (T1-T5) from the codex-efficiency eval campaign as skill/doc changes on codex-efficiency-fixes, grade each against its pre-registered criterion with the campaign's scorers, and cut one PR per passing treatment against dev.

nodes.label: Task 1 (T1): SDD worker-review prohibition
nodes.rationale: Depth-2 worker-spawned reviewers were 9/9 same-task duplicate reviews across four corpora in the codex-efficiency eval campaign; a reviewer a worker spawns duplicates the task review the controller dispatches at full cost and its approval counts for nothing in the process.

nodes.label: Task 2 (T3): codex-tools.md version-honest multi-agent rewrite
nodes.rationale: Five claims in the old multi-agent text were contradicted by the Codex CLI source: V2 has no close_agent; followup_task always reaches a child; role files attach via agent_type; full-history forks accept model/effort overrides; the V2 spawn allowlist hard-errors on non-V2 presets.

nodes.label: Task 3 (T2): codex-tools.md event-driven waiting section
nodes.rationale: 60-78% of wait_agent calls timed out across every measured corpus; waits are event subscriptions, so one long wait replaces dozens of polls at identical wake latency, and each short poll costs a tool call plus a context rebill.

nodes.label: Task 4 (T5): codex-tools.md model routing on spawns
nodes.rationale: Depth-2 child-issued spawns omitted model 2/2 at CLI 0.146; setting model without reasoning_effort silently resets effort to the model's default, not the session's, so every spawn must set both explicitly with a config-level backstop.

nodes.label: Task 5 (T4): brainstorming three-path router (variant C)
nodes.rationale: Measured pathology: the absolute hard-gate wording forced bounded tasks into the full two-document ritual 5/5 while a no-guidance control differentiated paths natively; the ceremony scales with the task, the approval gate never does, and the upgrade ratchet is one-way.

nodes.label: Amendment 1 (2026-07-30): first shared battery FAIL response
nodes.rationale: The first shared SDD battery (n=6) returned FAIL on T1/T2/T5: the no-subagents contract reached only the implementer prompt (a final reviewer spawned two sub-reviewers), and docs-only wait guidance produced no behavior change (65.1% vs 67.1% baseline timeouts).

nodes.label: Task 15 (T1-ext): no-subagents contract in all reviewer templates
nodes.rationale: The first fix-cycle battery moved the depth-2 leak from implementers (9/9 baseline to 0/6) to a final reviewer that spawned two sub-reviewers; the contract now reaches every dispatched role and joins the T1 PR with Task 1's commit.

nodes.label: Task 16 (T2-strong): wait discipline in the SDD controller text
nodes.rationale: Docs-only wait guidance in the platform reference changed nothing (65.1% vs 67.1% baseline wait-timeout rate); the discipline now lives in the controller loop the session actually re-reads, and joins the T2 PR.

nodes.label: Amendment 2 (2026-07-30): round-2 battery findings
nodes.rationale: Round 2: T2's long-wait fix eliminated wait timeouts (65.1% to 0.0%) but produced 20-38 min silent transcripts that starve graders and let one child in 51 vanish unnoticed; T4's bounded path killed the doc ritual (0 docs vs 2/rep dev baseline) but 2/3 bounded reps implemented before any approval.

nodes.label: Task 17 (T2 round 3): bounded waits + reconcile
nodes.rationale: Round 2 proved the long-wait mechanism (65.1% to 0.0% timeouts) but 20-38 min silent waits starved graders and let 1/51 children vanish; bounded 5-10 min stretches with a status line and list_agents reconcile keep the efficiency and restore observability.

nodes.label: Task 18 (T4 round 2): approval-gate teeth on the bounded path
nodes.rationale: Live ceremony battery: bounded reps produced zero doc ritual (the measured win) but 2/3 implemented before any approval turn; the bounded path now states the stop explicitly, enforcing the variant-C invariant without a new design decision.

nodes.label: Task 19: wait guidance - non-blocking delivery preferred
nodes.rationale: Blocking waits are the fallback for platforms that cannot wake an idle controller, not the default; harnesses with completion notifications never need to block at all, and no codex behavioral delta is expected since codex V2 cannot wake an idle controller.

nodes.label: Amendment 4 (2026-07-31): triggering-check findings
nodes.rationale: Task 12: gemini routed a new project architectural 3/3; claude triggered brainstorming 3/3 but self-classified the new project bounded 3/3 by reading 'existing, understood flow' as app-genre familiarity rather than presence of code in the repo; the codex leg was blocked on exhausted subscription credits.

nodes.label: Task 20: router tightening - bounded measures the repo
nodes.rationale: Claude Code classified a brand-new project bounded 3/3 (once while explicitly noting the repo was empty) by reading 'existing, understood flow' as genre familiarity; Gemini routed the same prompt architectural 3/3, so bounded is redefined as existing code in this repo.

nodes.label: Task 12b: triggering re-run (claude + gemini) and codex leg
No-subagents contract (implementers and reviewers never dispatch subagents)
nodes.rationale: A worker-spawned reviewer duplicates the task review the controller dispatches anyway - a full extra review seat per task - and its verdict counts for nothing in the process; a worker-spawned reviewer is a defect to flag, not rigor.

nodes.label: Event-subscription waiting (wait_agent is a subscription, not a poll)
nodes.rationale: A long wait wakes the moment a child produces mailbox activity, with the same latency as a short one; short-timeout polling buys nothing and costs a tool call and a context rebill per poll, and roughly two-thirds of measured wait calls were short polls that timed out.

nodes.label: Bounded wait stretches with reconciliation
nodes.rationale: A 5-10 minute bounded stretch keeps nearly all of a long wait's efficiency while guaranteeing a stuck or lost child is noticed within minutes rather than at the end of the session; after each stretch post one status line, run list_agents, and chase any child that finished without reporting.

nodes.label: Three-path classification (spike / bounded / architectural)
nodes.rationale: The request is classified before the first question and the classification is said out loud so the human partner can override it; when in doubt take the heavier path, and hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path one-way (stop and step up, never downgrade).

nodes.label: Approval-gate invariant (ceremony scales, approval never does)
nodes.rationale: Every path ends with the human partner approving intent before implementation; a todo list or one-function utility may have a two-sentence chat design, but it must be presented and approved - 'simple' tasks are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work, and what scales with simplicity is the artifact, never the approval.

nodes.label: Explicit model + reasoning_effort on every spawn with config backstop
nodes.rationale: Setting model alone is a trap because the child's effort silently resets to that model's default; a machine-level default_subagent_model/default_subagent_reasoning_effort backstop in ~/.codex/config.toml routes any slipped spawn to a deliberate tier instead of silently inheriting the session's most expensive model.

nodes.label: Append-only hypothesis log with pre-registration
nodes.rationale: Corrections are new dated entries, never edits, and every battery gets a pre-registration entry BEFORE it runs, so the log stays a non-revisable record of what was predicted versus what was measured.

nodes.label: Fix arm worktree (/tmp/sp-arm-fix)
nodes.rationale: Batteries run through the existing quorum container lanes against a detached worktree of the codex-efficiency-fixes branch, refreshed before every later battery so the arm SHA matches the commits under test.

nodes.label: Pre-registration rule (criterion logged before the battery runs)
nodes.rationale: Recording the criterion, matrix, and predictions before spending on a battery keeps the verdict honest - the treatment is graded against a number committed in advance, not one chosen after the results.

nodes.label: Privacy sweep rule (campaign name-sets grep before every commit)
nodes.rationale: Raw rollouts and session content never enter any repo; before every autoresearch/evals commit, staged text and the commit-message file are grep'd against the campaign name-sets (client names, hostnames, ticket IDs) so only oblique references survive.
